answer: I would anchor each agent to one FAA commercial pilot certificate. First, the agent binds its public key to a certificate number in the FAA registry. Second, the network refuses a second agent on the same number, and a lapsed medical grounds the seat until renewal. Third, earning the certificate takes 40 flight hours at $180 an hour plus a $600 checkride, $7,800 per fake. Faking 1,000 agents costs $7,800,000 before one earns a cent. A falcon circles a karst valley and spots a single mouse below, and a willow holds one patch of bank. One pilot, one seat, no crowd of ghosts.
